source.title: RedAgent: An Autonomous Agent for Context-Aware Red Teaming of LLM Jailbreaks
source.authors: Hui-Yu Xu; Wen-Hui Zhang; Zhi-Bo Wang; Feng Xiao; Rui Zheng; Zhong-Jie Ba; Kui Ren

record.file_problem: The text contains the full paper and appendix. The title in the paper differs slightly from the supplied title, but it is the RedAgent study.
record.tranche_reason: The study builds and evaluates a red-teaming attack system whose purpose is to induce harmful responses. Its attack-success results do not test fine-tuning effects, first-token concentration, or the specified opening-token bypass mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The reported ASR and example outputs measure results of deliberately applied jailbreak attacks. They are recorded as attack-efficacy findings, not as evidence of uninduced model behavior or of the claim versions. References to fine-tuning and the original safety paper do not report new fine-tuning results.
record.test_reason: This study builds and evaluates a black-box jailbreak red-teaming agent (RedAgent) and reports attack success rates against chat models and custom GPTs. It does not fine-tune models (V1, V2), measure per-token KL (V3), or test prefilling, suffix or decoding interventions on the response opening (V4). It does not localize safety weights (V5), probe the cause of shallowness (V6), or train deeper alignment (V7). It also does not use the shallow-alignment finding as a tool. Its only link to the original sources is borrowing Qi et al.'s GPT-4 judge rubric for scoring harmfulness. That is an evaluation instrument, not the finding, so cites_only/T6 fits better than the reader's uses_without_test/T4. All ASRs come from deliberately applied persuasive or context-aware jailbreak prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that RedAgent jailbreaks most black-box LLMs within about five queries, roughly twice as efficient as prior red-teaming methods with over 90% average success. They report finding 60 vulnerabilities in custom GPTs and claim that apps enhanced with external data or tools are more vulnerable than foundation models. That last claim is not tested by a controlled comparison.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and evaluates an autonomous, context-aware red-teaming agent using adaptive prompt strategies and memory. It does not reproduce fine-tuning, token-position KL measurement, or opening-token bypass experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack success varies by target model and application context. The paper also reports changes in RedAgent performance with memory capacity and memory-tag configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Context-aware persuasive jailbreak prompts reach 74-100% ASR across six chat models (Table I), versus 0-100% for baseline attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Iterative persuasion-based black-box jailbreaks elicit harmful responses from safety-trained chat models at high rates.

fits_no_version.finding: RedAgent reports 100% ASR on custom GPT applications in all six categories with under 3 queries on average. The authors infer that apps with external data or tools are more vulnerable than foundation models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM applications customized with external data or tools are more jailbreak-susceptible than their foundation models.

record.code_released: The paper says the experiments code will be made public after mitigation of known attack threats on the service.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing
record.problems: The reported harmful responses are induced by deliberate jailbreak prompts and therefore do not measure uninduced model behavior. The GPT application results are summarized by category without category sample counts in Table II. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional query-efficiency (ANQ) results and ablations on memory capacity and tags in Tables I–IV. They were left out because these metrics concern attack efficiency or RedAgent design, not the harmful-response outcome recorded here.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position analysis between aligned and base models.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix optimization or decoding manipulation. Persuasion-style prompts do not test the opening-token mechanism.
No analysis of the cause of shallowness.

record.verdict_notes: The only connection to the original sources is reuse of Qi et al. (arXiv:2310.03693) as the 1-5 harmfulness judge rubric. No uncertainty is reported. Table I says it was manually annotated. The query budget is inconsistent (40 in Table I, 60 in the Metrics text).

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal after fine-tuning.
No fine-tuning on benign data or measurement of its effect on harmful compliance.
The study evaluates context-aware jailbreak prompts, not compliant-start prefilling, suffixes as an intervention, decoding changes, or whether bypassing the first response tokens is causal.
No localization or editing of safety-related weights or ranks.
No test of whether training data or objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training to deepen safety behavior or evaluation of its persistence.
